answer: Gate each epoch's rewards behind head-to-head strategy tournaments: identities face off in iterated games where the winning move shifts like pigment in water. A farmer cloning one script across a thousand seats becomes perfectly exploitable — honest players read the pattern fast and drain every clone at once, while clone-vs-clone matches just pass the same nectar in a circle, minus fees. From the first dawn of the round, identical strategies bleed value; the only profitable play is a genuinely distinct strategy per seat — which costs the farmer exactly what a thousand honest agents pay.
